solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food bank donation possibly protecting large family (4)

indicatorNotes.protecting: the can wraps around the L, shielding it

blocks.note: a tin of food is a typical food bank donation
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A charity tin of food keeping a big family going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags that a can is only one example of a food bank donation.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a Scottish clan is a group of families claiming one common ancestor.

entries.clue: Name one work where, ultimately, she was an inspiration? (8)

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them

annotation.surface: A question about naming a work that a woman inspired.
annotation.walkthrough: Calliope was the Greek Muse of epic poetry; Muses were the classic source of a poet's inspiration, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: As a Muse, Calliope literally was the inspiration for poets.

entries.clue: A skill in fine material giving lots of options (1,2,5)

indicatorNotes.in: something 'in' another is held inside it, so ART sits within LACE

blocks.note: an art is a skill, as in 'the art of conversation'

annotation.surface: Craftsmanship in a fine fabric that opens up many possibilities.
annotation.walkthrough: The skill is placed inside the fabric, and the plain A is stuck on the front.
annotation.definitionFit: An à la carte menu lets diners choose freely from many separately priced dishes.

entries.clue: March issue taken on by extremely sensible reporter from far-flung places (5,5)

indicatorNotes.taken on by: PACE PROB is taken inside S…E
indicatorNotes.extremely: take just the two extremes of 'sensible'

blocks.note: first and last letters of SensiblE

annotation.surface: A sensible journalist taking on a March story from distant lands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' looks like a journalist, but a probe reports data back from deep space.
annotation.definitionFit: A space probe sends back reports from distant parts of the solar system.

entries.clue: Lacking faith, people are generally always negative at first (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each of the five words

blocks.note: initials of People Are Generally Always Negative

annotation.surface: Faithless people tend to be negative about everything.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sweeping opinion, which disguises that the five words are only there for their initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A pagan is someone outside the main religions, so without the faith in question.

entries.clue: Drove that lady in Paris to join daughter after school (9)

blocks.note: a comp is a comprehensive, the standard British state secondary school
D = daughter, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A woman drove to Paris to collect her daughter after school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drove' reads as driving a car, but it means forced.
annotation.definitionFit: To drive someone to do something is to compel them.

entries.clue: Clears up after disordered party boat? (8,5)

indicatorNotes.disordered: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: Someone tidying up after a rowdy boat party.
annotation.walkthrough: The disorder belongs to the letters, not to the party; the question mark covers calling a pleasure craft a party boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A pleasure craft is a boat used for leisure rather than work.

entries.clue: Might this affect hearing over time? Yes, correct! (6)

blocks.note: O = over, as on a cricket scorecard
'it is!' is an emphatic yes, that's right

annotation.surface: A quiz question about hearing loss with age, answered with an eager yes.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue's own answer, 'Yes, correct!', is part of the wordplay: IT IS.
annotation.definitionFit: Otitis, inflammation of the ear, can impair hearing.

entries.clue: Figure having great influence from the second point on (6)

indicatorNotes.from the second point on: start at the second letter, dropping the first

blocks.note: weighty = influential; drop its first letter W

annotation.surface: An influential person who matters from a certain point onwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person of note, which the influence supports, but it is a number.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'figure' means a number written in digits, and 80 is one.

entries.clue: Being a landlord, say, is gratifying, but not at first (7)

indicatorNotes.not at first: the word is 'not' there at its first position, so its opening letter is missing

blocks.note: pleasing = gratifying; drop its first letter P

annotation.surface: Owning rental property is satisfying, though not in the early days.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks that leasing is one example of what a landlord does.
annotation.definitionFit: A landlord's business is leasing property to tenants.

entries.clue: Varied comment about very first bit of quote? (8,5)

annotation.surface: Some mixed remarks about how a quotation begins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of' but asks for rearrangement; 'Varied' is fodder, not the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A quotation opens with an inverted comma, its very first mark.

entries.clue: Satisfying company get-together(7)

blocks.note: read as a verb, as in satisfying a demand or a deadline
a gathering of colleagues around a boardroom table

annotation.surface: A pleasing office social.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Satisfying' reads as an adjective praising the gathering, but it is the verb, as in satisfying requirements.
annotation.definitionFit: To satisfy demands is to meet them, and a company get-together is a meeting.

entries.clue: Earlier on, fashionable parts of Nevada changed to accommodate casinos, primarily (2,7)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters of NEVADA are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to accommodate: the rearranged letters hold the C

annotation.surface: Stylish areas of Nevada were redeveloped long ago to make room for casinos.
annotation.walkthrough: The Nevada and casinos picture is Las Vegas; C goes between ADVAN and E.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done in advance is done earlier on.

entries.clue: Small, lean bird (5)

annotation.surface: A little skinny bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like thin, which fits a small bird, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The stilt is a long-legged wading bird.

entries.clue: Comic actor looks to take on curt, vacuous Liberal (5,7)

indicatorNotes.to take on: PEERS takes TERSE LL inside it
indicatorNotes.vacuous: empty 'Liberal' of its middle, leaving LL

annotation.surface: A comedian seems to be tackling a short-tempered, empty-headed Liberal politician.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers was the British comedian of The Goon Show and the Pink Panther films.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Sellers, star of Dr Strangelove and the Pink Panther films, is among the best-known screen comedians.

entries.clue: Unusual artiste — he is the most vulgar (9)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: the letters are arranged in an unusual way

annotation.surface: A strange performer declared the crudest of them all.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits the fodder so it reads as a verdict on the artiste.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse, so the earthiest is the most vulgar.

entries.clue: Welcome ordinary people accepting king’s funny business (8)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept something is to take it in, so LAITY receives R inside itself

blocks.note: the laity are people who aren't clergy

annotation.surface: Common folk greeting a monarch's comic antics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny business' usually means something shady, but here it is plain laughter.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful stretch: 'funny business' is usually shady dealing, taken literally here as the stuff of laughter.

entries.clue: Like lofty entertainment on the run? (2-6)

blocks.note: 'lofty' means literally aloft: the films shown to passengers on a plane

annotation.surface: A grand show put on while escaping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lofty' looks like highbrow, but it means literally high up, on a plane.
annotation.definitionFit: In-flight describes what happens aboard a plane; in flight also means fleeing.

entries.clue: Expert in discounting forged artwork? (12)

annotation.surface: A specialist in spotting fakes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expert in discounting forged artwork' reads as someone who rejects fakes; the question mark admits a reproduction is not always a forgery.
annotation.definitionFit: A reproduction is a copy of an artwork, which passed off as original becomes a forgery.

entries.clue: Tees maybe beneath key item in golf bag (6)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down entry, RIVER sits below D

blocks.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

annotation.surface: Golf tees tucked under the main club in the bag.
annotation.walkthrough: Tees are golf pegs in the surface, which makes 'Tees' very hard to read as the river.
annotation.definitionFit: A driver is the golf club used off the tee.

entries.clue: Bring out drug sanctioned by law (6)

annotation.surface: Releasing a drug that has been legally approved.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a medicine brought to market; 'Bring out' means draw forth.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: you draw out, or bring out, an answer or a reaction by questioning.

entries.clue: Orwell piece periodically taken as something of historic interest (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: take every other letter, at regular intervals

annotation.surface: An article by George Orwell now regarded as a period piece.
annotation.walkthrough: Start at the second letter of 'Orwell' and keep going across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past.

entries.clue: Enjoy yourself, as many sports require you to? (4,1,4)

annotation.definition2: as many sports require you to

blocks.note: an idiom for having a wonderful time, as at a grand dance

blocks.clueFragment: as many sports require you to
blocks.note: you can't play football or tennis without having a ball

annotation.surface: Advice to have fun, as sport demands.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Having a ball is an idiom for enjoying yourself enormously.

entries.clue: Part of book really devoid of excitement at the beginning (5)

indicatorNotes.devoid of: something devoid of a thing lacks it, so the E is taken out

blocks.note: 'ever so' = really, as in 'ever so kind'; drop the E
first letter of Excitement, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A section of a book that is dull from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Removing E from EVER SO happens to take away its first letter too, echoing 'at the beginning'.
annotation.definitionFit: The verso is the left-hand page of a book.

entries.clue: Aristocratic Frenchman’s struggle involving company minutes and report’s conclusion (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to enfold or include, so VIE wraps around CO M T

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

annotation.surface: A French noble battling over board minutes and the end of a report.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' is read as 'has', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: French title: the rank just below a comte (count), equal to a British viscount.

entries.clue: Group split apart by excessive corruption (7)

indicatorNotes.split apart by: RING is opened up and OTT pushed in

blocks.note: a ring is a group, e.g. a spy ring

annotation.surface: A gang torn apart by extreme corruption.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corruption' reads as graft, fitting the gang, but it is decay.
annotation.definitionFit: Rotting is decomposition, the physical sense of corruption.

entries.clue: Withdrawal almost reminiscent of past performance (10)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so RETRO stops one letter short

blocks.note: retro = in a past style, minus its last letter O
action = performance, as in a machine's action

annotation.surface: Pulling back from a show that recalls earlier glories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost' sits before 'reminiscent', so the trim applies to RETRO, not ACTION.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: taking back a claim, as a newspaper does when it prints a correction.

entries.clue: Money obtained from somewhat finicky ATM (4)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: take only some of the letters

annotation.surface: Getting cash from a fussy cash machine.
annotation.walkthrough: The kyat is the currency of Myanmar (Burma), a word most solvers know only from crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Myanmar's currency, divided into 100 pyas.
